# What does this PR do?
Preserves evaluation semantics after a training CUDA graph has been captured.

  Capture a separate validation graph instead of replaying a graph captured with training and grad mode enabled. This
  prevents capture-time Python branches and buffer mutations, such as MoE router token-count
  accumulation, from being replayed during validation.

## Contribution process

- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests

- [x] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

issue_comments.body:
Light review — traced the new validation capture/replay paths. The design looks sound: the eager fallbacks for pre-capture / shape-mismatch / grad-enabled eval mirror the pre-existing fallbacks, `preserve_model_state` keeps `buffer_backup` and `saved_fp8_tensors` symmetric (and incidentally fixes FP4 being saved but never restored), the fresh `ArgMetadata` inputs carry no `cg_buffer_metadata` so `fwd_buffer_reuse_ref_count` accounting is untouched, and holding detached `outputs` before `_weakref_forward_buffers(False)` correctly keeps output storage owned. Test coverage is good.

One thing worth a look:

**With PP > 1, one validation graph is captured per microbatch runner but only the first is ever replayed.**

`_create_cudagraphs` captures a val graph for *every* grad-enabled runner:

```python
# megatron/core/transformer/cuda_graphs.py:717
for runner in dict.fromkeys(g[0] for g in cls.cudagraph_record):
    if runner.grad_enabled:
        runner.create_val_graph()
```

but the selection in `__call__` scans `self.cudagraph_runners` in order and — deliberately, per the test comment — never rotates the list:

```python
# megatron/core/transformer/cuda_graphs.py:2154
runner = next(
    (r.val_runner for r in self.cudagraph_runners if ...), None
)
```

When `reuse_cudagraphs` is False (`pp.size() > 1`) there is one runner per microbatch, and all of them were recorded from the same training signature, so `get_mismatch_errors` never rejects index 0. The selected runner is therefore always `cudagraph_runners[0].val_runner`, and the remaining `num_microbatches - 1` validation graphs per graphed module are captured, hold their output buffers strongly for the life of the run, and are never replayed.

Correctness looks fine — the forward-only schedules send each stage output before the next microbatch's forward, so a single shared val graph per module is safe — so this is purely wasted capture time and pool memory, scaling with `num_microbatches × num_graphed_layers`.

Since the capture loop lives on `_CudagraphGlobalRecord` and has no manager grouping, the cheap fix is probably to skip runners that would produce a duplicate val graph, e.g.:

```python
# Backwards have released the training activations, so validation can reuse their pool.
# Validation replay never rotates `cudagraph_runners`, so it always selects the first
# runner's graph; capturing one per microbatch would only waste pool memory.
captured_val_keys = set()
for runner in dict.fromkeys(g[0] for g in cls.cudagraph_record):
    key = (id(runner.base_module), runner.func)
    if runner.grad_enabled and key not in captured_val_keys:
        captured_val_keys.add(key)
        runner.create_val_graph()
```

(keying on `runner.func` as well as the module matters for the method-wrapped form, where two managers can share one `base_module` under different `function_name`s.)

Alternatively, if the per-microbatch graphs are intentional as headroom for a future rotating validation path, a comment saying so would help — the `PP creates one runner per microbatch` test comment currently reads as if all of them are exercised, and `test_separate_evaluation_graphs` asserts over every entry of `val_runners` without distinguishing the one that actually replays.

Light review — the fix looks correct in shape (grad-mode branches and buffer mutations are frozen at capture, so replaying a training graph under `eval()`/`no_grad()` is wrong), and it also incidentally avoids rotating `self.cudagraph_runners` during validation. Three things:

**1. Non-`nn.Module` `base_module` (inline comment).** `megatron_module.training` is read unconditionally; see the inline note.

**2. Stale comment + missing doc update.** `megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py:1614` still says `# Training and validation mode CUDA graphs.` above the `_should_call_local_cudagraph` check. With this change the `local` path no longer replays graphs during validation — `_should_call_local_cudagraph` still returns `True`, but the manager now falls through to eager. Suggest updating that comment, and adding a line to `docs/user-guide/features/cuda_graph.md` under the `local` section noting that eval/validation runs eager. That is relevant because the doc explicitly calls out validation-mode graphs for `full_iteration` (lines 117-118), so readers will reasonably assume `local` behaves the same. The PR checklist claims documentation was added, but the diff has none.

**3. Test covers only the `self.func` branch.** `test_training_graph_falls_back_to_eager_during_evaluation` uses `function_name="project"`, so it exercises `return self.func(*args, **kwargs)`. The default production configuration is `function_name=None` (whole-`TransformerLayer` capture via `GraphableMegatronModule.__init__`), which takes the other branch — `super(MegatronModule, megatron_module).__call__(*args, **kwargs)` — and that branch is untested. A second case (e.g. a `TransformerBlock`, or a `_GradModeBufferModule` with a plain `cudagraph_manager` attribute and no `function_name`) would cover the path most users actually hit. It would also be worth asserting that a subsequent training-mode forward still replays the graph (`training_forwards` increments, runner status intact) after the eager eval pass, since that is the invariant the early `return` depends on.

Light review — the fix and the added unit tests look right for the standard `evaluate()` path. Two things worth confirming before merge, both about workloads that are **forward-only but not eval-semantics**, where replay was previously intended.

**1. `--freeze-all-layers` loses replay while still paying for capture**

`megatron/training/training.py:2358` runs the *training* forward/backward under `torch.no_grad()` with the model still in `train()` mode. With the new condition (`cuda_graphs.py:2082-2084`):

- `module_is_training` = True, `torch.is_grad_enabled()` = False, `is_in_checkpoint_fwd` = False → `can_replay_training_graph` is False → eager.
- But the pre-capture branch is unchanged (`elif self.training or is_in_checkpoint_fwd:` at `cuda_graphs.py:2152`), so graphs are still **recorded and created** on the first iteration — they just never get replayed. Net effect: eager execution plus the full graph memory footprint.

Note the capture in that case happens with grad disabled too, so replay was semantically correct there — the mismatch this PR targets only exists when the graph was captured with grad *enabled*. Gating on the captured runner grad mode rather than the ambient one would keep that case working:

```python
            is_explicit_inference = is_inference_mode or self._inline_capture
            module_is_training = getattr(megatron_module, "training", self.training)
            grad_active = torch.is_grad_enabled() or is_in_checkpoint_fwd
            captured_with_grad = any(r.grad_enabled for r in self.cudagraph_runners)
            can_replay_training_graph = module_is_training and (
                grad_active or not captured_with_grad
            )
```

(with a comment noting that a graph captured with grad disabled has the same Python branches as a no-grad forward, so replaying it preserves semantics.)

**2. Stale comment in the RL logprobs path**

`megatron/rl/rl_utils.py:2177-2180` sets `model.eval()` *specifically* to reuse the training-captured graph — the comment there says "this path reuses the forward pass from training after it has been captured on the 1st iteration" — and its callers wrap it in `torch.no_grad()` (`rl_utils.py:2421`, `2441`, `2456`). After this PR that path falls back to eager on every logprob pass. That is arguably the *correct* new behavior (the router counters this PR protects would have been accumulating there too), but the comment now documents the opposite, and it is a per-step hot path — please confirm the perf change is acceptable and update the comment either way.

Nothing else — no process-group issues, the docs update reads accurately, and the parametrized `wrapped_method`/`whole_module` test covers both manager forms.

Light review. The eager-eval fallback and the tests look right for the standard `evaluate()` path, but the new gate is broader than the PR description and docs claim, and it silently turns off graph replay for two paths that intentionally relied on it.

**1. RL reference-logprob path loses training-graph replay**

`megatron/rl/rl_utils.py:2177-2180` deliberately enters eval + `no_grad` *specifically so it can replay the training graph*. Its own comment says so: "Avoid self.training checks which will trigger cudagraph capture; this path reuses the forward pass from training after it has been captured on the 1st iteration." It then calls `model.eval()` followed by `get_logprobs(..., no_grad=True)`.

Under the new gate this call has `module_is_training=False`, `torch.is_grad_enabled()=False`, `is_in_checkpoint_fwd=False`, and is neither `is_inference_mode` nor `_inline_capture` — so `can_replay_training_graph` is False and it falls back to eager. Replaying here is the point of `--rl-training-cuda-graphs`: when that flag is off, `rl_utils.py:2285-2289` already deletes `cudagraph_manager` via `toggle_cuda_graphs`, so the manager only survives at this call site when the user explicitly asked for replay.

This is a silent perf regression rather than a correctness one, which makes it easy to miss in CI. Worth either exempting this path explicitly (e.g. an opt-in flag on the manager, similar to `_inline_capture`) or confirming the RL owners are fine with the slowdown.

**2. `--freeze-all-layers` training also falls back**

`_forward_backward_grad_context()` (`megatron/training/training.py:2349-2360`) runs a *training* step under `torch.no_grad()` with the model still in `train()` mode. That gives `module_is_training=True`, `grad_enabled=False` -> `can_replay_training_graph` False -> eager. Previously this replayed.

That may well be the desired outcome, but it means the doc paragraph is narrower than the code:

> A graph captured during training is not replayed by standard evaluation under `model.eval()` with autograd disabled.

The actual condition is "the module is not in training mode **or** autograd is disabled (outside a checkpoint-forward)". Suggest rewording so users grepping for why replay stopped can find it, e.g.:

```
A graph captured during training is only replayed while the module is in training mode with
autograd enabled (or during a checkpointed recompute forward). Standard evaluation under
`model.eval()`, and forward-only training with autograd disabled, run eagerly so that
capture-time Python branches and mutable-buffer updates retain their eager semantics.
Explicit inference CUDA graphs remain unaffected.
```

**3. Test coverage gap**

`test_training_graph_falls_back_to_eager_during_evaluation` covers the fallback well (both the wrapped-method and whole-module forms), but nothing asserts the *negative* side of the new gate — that replay is still taken where it should be. A cheap addition to the same class: after `create_cudagraphs()`, run one `train()` + `torch.no_grad()` forward and assert the intended behaviour explicitly, so a future tightening of this condition cannot quietly disable replay for the frozen-teacher and RL cases above.

**Minor**

`megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py:1615` — the added comment starts lowercase and reads as a fragment next to the line above it; consider capitalizing it into a full sentence.

**Light review**

Reviewed the diff against `skills/mcore-testing`. The mechanism is sound — separate forward-only graphs sharing the training pool, with an eager fallback for unmatched shapes/autograd-enabled — and the unit-test coverage is genuinely thorough (PP=1/2, wrapped-method and whole-module capture, eval-before-capture, pool-address verification, in-place aliasing, post-`delete_cuda_graphs` behavior). Three inline comments, one of which I think is a real bug:
1. **FP8/FP4 state is not saved/restored around the validation capture** (`cuda_graphs.py:1250`) — the backup/restore blocks in `create_fwd_graph` are gated on `self.training and torch.is_grad_enabled()`, both false for the val runner, yet the capture still runs under a live fp8 context. The extra warmup+capture forwards mutate TE amax history with no rollback. This is the finding I would most want addressed before merge; the added tests do not cover fp8 (the `check_fp8_support` import in the test file is unused by the new class).
2. **Val replay never sets `runner.status`** (`cuda_graphs.py:2147-2150`) — correct today by construction, but the training path sets it explicitly and this one relies on an undocumented invariant.
3. **Val graphs are captured unconditionally** (`cuda_graphs.py:717-720`) — jobs with `--eval-iters 0` pay double capture time and extra graph memory for graphs they never replay.

**PR description is stale.** The body describes the previous approach:
> Ordinary evaluation under `model.eval()` and `torch.no_grad()` now falls back to eager execution instead of replaying a graph captured with training and grad mode enabled.

The commit on this branch (`032dae9 fix: capture separate CUDA graphs for validation`) captures dedicated validation graphs instead, with eager only as the fallback for unmatched inputs or autograd-enabled eval. The title (`fix: preserve eager evaluation semantics after CUDA graph capture`) reads the same way. Worth updating both so reviewers and `git log` readers are not misled about which strategy landed.

**Docs.** `docs/user-guide/features/cuda_graph.md` accurately describes the new behavior, including the ordering constraint ("Run validation between completed training steps, after all training backwards have finished"). Consider noting there that the extra graphs are always captured, if finding 3 is not gated.
